A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same rCM research, with matching authors, methods, and principal experiments. All pages, including Appendices A–F, are readable; text extraction and visual inspection support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original diffusion-distillation experiments on Cosmos-Predict2 and Wan2.1, including GenEval and VBench results in Tables 1–3 and supplementary experiments in Appendix E.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds a loss-weight ablation and further qualitative comparison samples.

M1.justification: The combined consistency/DMD objective, rollout strategy, teacher wrapping, and Algorithms 1–2 are retained. Section 4.2 explicitly clarifies full-JVP computation with FP32 time embeddings for large models and video; it does not establish a changed procedure. The Equation (5) correction aligns with the algorithm already present in v1.

E1.justification: Both retain GenEval text-to-image and VBench text-to-video/image-to-video coverage, including the existing 720p Cosmos evaluation. The additional illustrative prompts support the loss-weight analysis within retained video-generation coverage. The revised data-source citation does not establish changed data, and autoregressive video is discussed only as future work.

E2.justification: Figure 1 adds SiD and teacher samples to the Wan2.1-1.3B qualitative comparison previously displaying sCM, DMD2, and rCM. SiD was already discussed in v1 but was absent from this displayed comparison. Comparator membership in Tables 1–3 and the appendix sCM/sCTM comparison remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 4 revises pG, and the Cosmos pD distributions, from normal sampling of z to normal sampling of log z, also specifying variance as 1.6 squared. This changes the reported setting without establishing reruns. The new four-step Wan2.1-1.3B ablation specifies four lambda values, batch size 64, and 10,000 training iterations.

E4.justification: V2 adds a targeted sensitivity study testing how the score-loss weight controls quality and diversity, using lambda values 1, 0.1, 0.01, and 0.001 in Figure 7. Figure 1 also expands the existing diversity case study. The sampling-step, sCM/sCTM, and numerical-precision analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V2 explicitly documents five different generation seeds per prompt for the new lambda study; v1 already displayed five random samples in Figure 1. This is a limited addition of seed information. GenEval still repeats 553 prompts four times, and neither version reports training-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their numerical results. New Figure 7 reports VBench scores of 84.32, 84.57, 84.43, and 82.68 for lambda values 1, 0.1, 0.01, and 0.001, respectively. These are added ablation results, not improvements over matched v1 experiments. Figure 1 adds teacher and SiD qualitative outputs.

T1.justification: Equation (5) changes the coefficient on the student-minus-teacher term from +cos(t) to -cos(t), correcting its inconsistency with the derivative expression in Section 2.2 and Algorithm 1. The remaining derivations, including the appendix attention-JVP and consistency-trajectory mathematics, are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract modestly qualifies the quality comparison from 'matches or surpasses' DMD2 to 'generally matches.' The introduction retains the stronger comparison, while the principal claims about scalability, diversity, 1–4-step generation, and acceleration remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the lambda sweep as a quality/diversity trade-off and identifies 0.01 as the smallest tested order-of-magnitude weight preserving quality. It narrows generalization wording to the models and tasks used. The introduction also proposes causal-teacher consistency distillation as a possible complement to Self-Forcing, explicitly for future exploration.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 clarifies the full-JVP/FP32 implementation, Table 4 corrects time-sampling specifications, and Section 5.2 supplies the new ablation's training budget. Appendix F documents three additional visualization prompts. The project access link and existing infrastructure and optimizer documentation are retained.

R1.justification: The introduction adds DDRL, expands the conceptual connection to the already cited DDO, and explains a potential relationship to Self-Forcing. The earlier NVIDIA Cosmos report citation is replaced by Ali et al. (2025). These are limited positioning changes; Appendix A's related-work discussion is retained.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the abstract and portions of the introduction, adds explanatory footnotes and an LLM-writing disclosure, and replaces the preprint header with the conference-publication header. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is reorganized around additional teacher/SiD panels, Figure 3 gains teacher/student labels, Figure 7 adds the ablation display, and Table 5 expands the prompt list. Figures 4 and 6 move, and existing appendix figures are renumbered. The principal benchmark tables retain their structure.

improvement.justification: The new lambda ablation better supports the previously asserted default-weight choice, while Figure 1 strengthens the qualitative comparisons. Correcting Equation (5) and Table 4 and clarifying full-JVP computation improve mathematical consistency and reproducibility. These provide a limited overall gain: the principal benchmark results are unchanged, and the added diversity evidence remains qualitative and concentrated on one model scale.
